title: Staged changelog & deprecation-ramp: customer-facing upgrade notes and comms templates
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a repeatable, customer-friendly upgrade notes and deprecation ramp template plus automation hooks for generating staged changelogs targeted to customer tiers (self-serve, dedicated, private). The output must include: 1) succinct release notes for immediate inbox communication, 2) a migration guide for engineers, 3) deprecation timeline messaging (30/14/7 day windows), and 4) per-tier escalation templates for high-impact breaking changes. Integrate with existing release automation (release-scribe pipeline) to auto-populate changelog sections from GitHub PR labels and runtime compatibility metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Public-facing one-paragraph release summary that can be used in emails and console banners
Detailed migration guide with code snippets, configuration diffs, and rollback steps hosted in Confluence/Drive
Deprecation ramp messaging with clear dates and actions for 30/14/7 day notices for both hosted and private customers
Automated script (release-scribe) hooks documented with example commands and sample payloads
Templates for three customer tiers (self-serve, reserved/dedicated, private/VPC) with escalation contacts
Sign-off from Legal/Trust and Product Security for wording on data retention and compatibility guarantees
changelog_template:
[Summary]
- One-line: user-visible change and impact
- Why: short rationale
- Affected APIs/SDKs: endpoints, params, SDK versions
- Migration notes: quick steps + link to full guide
- Rollback path: how to opt-out or pin previous runtime
- Contact & escalation: support@redwood.ai + account team link
deprecation_ramp_policy: Phase 1 (30 days): public announcement + banner + email to admins. Phase 2 (14 days): targeted account notifications to active callers + guided migration call offered for high-usage customers. Phase 3 (7 days): final reminder and automated safe-fallback policy enabled for Dedicated customers if configured in runtime. Last resort: hard deprecation only after approvals and an archived snapshot of the deprecated runtime for emergency restores.
communication_templates:
Self-serve email (30 days):
Subject: Upcoming change to Redwood runtime that may affect tokenization behavior
Body: Hi {org_admin}, on {date} we will roll out runtime-1.24 which adjusts tokenization heuristics for improved cost/latency. Most apps will see no change. If you use custom token-level metrics or exact token counts for billing, see the migration guide: {link}. Contact support@redwood.ai if you have questions.

Dedicated customer email (30/14/7 cadence):
Subject: Action recommended: runtime-1.24 upgrade window and optional migration support
Body: Dear {account_owner}, we plan to upgrade your Dedicated pool to runtime-1.24 between {start_window} and {end_window}. Changes include kernel selection improvements and a minor API response field rename. We strongly recommend testing in your staging cluster. Schedule a migration call: {board_link}. If no action is taken, we will apply a non-breaking compatibility shim. For breaking opt-in features we will not enable them without consent.

Private deployment advisory (policy + checklist):
Subject: Advisory: runtime-1.24 available for private deployments
Body: For private customers, runtime updates are delivered via the Private Updater package. Follow the migration checklist: backup config, run upgrade dry-run, validate SLOs for 24h, roll forward. See the private migration guide: {drive_link}. Contact CSM: {csm_email} for scheduled assistance.
automation_integration_notes: Work with Eng: add two new labels 'release-note:breaking' and 'runtime-compat:runtime-1.24' to PRs. release-scribe will collect PRs with those labels into 'Breaking changes' and 'Compatibility notes' sections. Provide example GH action: .github/workflows/release-scribe.yml -> uses scripts/release_scribe.py --runtime runtime-1.24 --output changelog.md. Documented in Confluence: /ReleaseOps/Release-Scribe-Automation.
migration_guide_outline:
1) Overview and TL;DR
2) What changed (behavioral + API) with small examples
3) Step-by-step migration (SDK bump, config flags, runtime pinning)
4) Test plan (requests to run, logs to inspect)
5) Rollback instructions
6) Common pitfalls and FAQ
7) Contact & SLA notes
